title: [recoverability][observability] the transcript archive's failures are recorded: the Bridge records archive.failed {native, reason} when a transcript's pass fails for a reason other than the one recorded last, and archive.resumed {native, copied} at the first pass that copies after one, a failed record tried again under the same key
prompt:
Spawn, objective 179 [recoverability][observability] (projects-47, 2026-11-14: 175's split (a); the shape in sync/design-179-archive-failed.md b49db0c6, accepted by the lead with archive.resumed, and rev-e's five early notes settled; split on 2026-11-15 at the lead's word into 179, the Bridge's records, and 193, the alert; reviewers rev-e, then cc-astra): the transcript archive's failures are recorded. After [175]: it builds on 175's archive code, so it can be pushed only once the fleet has built 175.

Line: core line 6 [recoverability]; [observability].

Why. 175 fails closed: a pass that cannot have every credential value, or whose copy fails, copies nothing. Today the only signs are a loop log warning (said once per change of error) and the progress record's behind_ms, in a file under `<root>-progress`. Nothing raises an alert, so an archive can fall behind for days, until Claude Code's cleanup deletes the transcript it lacks.

What changes:
(1) crates/spawn-core/src/event.rs: two event kinds, on the session's own stream, source bridge.
  - `archive.failed {native, reason}`: one transcript's pass copied nothing. reason is the error as the loop's warning says it (paths and errors, never a value: 175's rule), at most ARCHIVE_REASON_MAX = 500 characters, cut on a character boundary.
  - `archive.resumed {native, copied}`: the first pass that copied after an archive.failed of the same transcript. copied is how far the transcript offset moved in that pass.
(2) crates/spawn-core/src/bridge.rs: `Bridge::record_archive_pass`, called after each copy on both paths (a live execution's pass and an ended execution's retry). Per (agent, native) it keeps what the store was told (ArchiveEvents) and records on a change only:
  - archive.failed when the pass failed for a reason other than the one recorded last;
  - archive.resumed when it copied after a recorded failure;
  - nothing while the state is what the store holds.
  A first transcripts::MASK_CHANGED (175 R3: a rotation between the mask and the read, copied on the next pass) records nothing; a second in a row records archive.failed with it. The event's key, `archive:<native>:<ms>:<n>`, is made when the change is first tried and kept until the log takes it: a failed append is warned and retried at the next pass under the same key (stored once), and a newer change replaces a pending one. The keys are never reused after a restart. The loop's warning is unchanged.
  After a restart (R2, rev-e's F1), the Bridge reads each transcript's last archive event back as it folds the log (fold_archive_event seeds ArchiveEvents.failed): a pass that still fails the same way records nothing, and the first pass that copies records archive.resumed, on the live path and on an ended execution's retry alike. Before R2 a restarted Bridge said a failure again, and never ended a failure fixed while the loop was down.
  Test helper: crates/spawn-core/src/memory.rs (feature testing) `MemoryStore::lose_next_archive_answer`: the next archive record is stored and then answered with an error, as a log whose answer is lost after it took the event.
Owner part: rsi/scenarios/179.sh (the contract).

Not in it: the alert (objective 193, after [175, 179]), which reads these events; and what the archive copies.

Cost: nothing is read on a polled path; the Bridge appends an event only when a transcript's archive state changes (none in a healthy hour).

170 note: 170 (held) adds a LIMITED table of event text fields. Whichever of 170 and 179 lands second adds ("archive.failed", "reason") at 500 there, so the cut and the store agree.

Files: crates/spawn-core/src/{event.rs, bridge.rs, memory.rs}; rsi/scenarios/179.sh (owner).
Size (measured on the compiled branch against 175's tip, split at `mod tests`): code 176 (bridge.rs 148, event.rs 28), tests 171 (bridge.rs), the test helper 18 (memory.rs); R2 adds code 18 and tests 62 (bridge.rs), so code 194 and tests 233; 179.sh 697 (owner).

Acceptance: rsi/scenarios/179.sh, black box, on 175.sh's world (a real `spawn loop`, one ephemeral worker on a fake engine, a made-up credential file and a stand-in location tool that lists the file as unreadable when it cannot read it).
(1) The credential rotated and its file unreadable, a BB:SAY turn: within 20 s the store holds one archive.failed, its reason naming the credential file's path; no archive event holds a form or a part of a value.
(2) A second turn, still unreadable: 8 s after it, still one archive.failed.
(3) The loop killed and started again by its runner (as systemd does), still unreadable, a third turn: 8 s after it, still one archive.failed (read back, not said again), naming the file, and no archive.resumed.
(4) The file readable again: within 20 s one archive.resumed, of the same native session; no archive event holds a form of a value.
(5) Unreadable again and a turn: a second archive.failed. The loop killed, the file made readable before its runner starts it again (the runner waits 5 s), and a turn: within 20 s a second archive.resumed, still two archive.failed.
On 175 alone and on main 6796e8c6, 179.sh exits 1 at (1). On 179 R1 (7ddd1f63) it exits 1 at (3): the restarted Bridge said the failure again.

Tests (unit):
- bridge: a failure is recorded on a change and its end once; one stale mask records nothing and two in a row record a failure; the reason is cut to its limit; a failed record is tried again under the same key (the log took it, its answer was lost: one event); a failure recorded before a restart is ended by the restarted Bridge (still failing after a restart: nothing more; copying after a second restart: one archive.resumed).
No test is renamed or dropped.

R3 (cc-astra A78, through the lead): a transcript gone (deleted by Claude Code's cleanup) while its failure is recorded, and the archive lacking lines of it, never reads resumed. archive_to says the file was gone (Archived.gone); copy_transcript returns Ok(false) for a gone file, keeps behind_ms and records archive_failed; record_archive_pass, given gone, records nothing new for it. Test (unit, bridge): a_transcript_gone_with_lines_unarchived_never_reads_resumed. The A78 mutants (the copy or the record ignoring gone) are killed by that unit test and by 179.sh (6) (rev-e's case): unreadable, a turn, a third archive.failed; the session's transcript removed under the scratch SPAWN_CLAUDE_PROJECTS and the file made readable. 20 s later there are still two archive.resumed, and the store's last archive event of that native session is archive.failed.

R4 (rev-g's F1 on R3): the guard no longer depends on the log. A transcript gone with lines the archive lacks stays behind whatever the log holds. A failure recorded, or an archive.failed still waiting to be taken (its answer lost), stands and is retried under its key. With neither (a first MASK_CHANGED records nothing), the loss is recorded as archive.failed with reason ARCHIVE_GONE, "the transcript was removed before the archive had every line of it", once (193's alert fires on it). Test (unit, bridge): a_transcript_removed_with_lines_unarchived_is_a_failure_whatever_the_log_holds (a lost answer; a first stale mask). Its mutants are unit-only. The waiting append and the first stale mask must both fall between a failing pass and the file's removal, a race a scenario cannot place, so the unit test places them with the in-memory log.
